definition: Carpathian Flysch Belt is an arcuate [tectonic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plate_tectonics) included in the megastructural elevation of the [Carpathians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpathians) on the external periphery of the mountain chain.
Carriacou Formation is a [geologic formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(geology)) in [Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenada).
Carrizo-Wilcox Aquifer is an [aquifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquifer) in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas), United States.
Casa Grande is the official state [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil) of [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona).

Cascadia Channel is the most extensive [deep-sea channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep-sea_channel) currently known (as of 1969) of the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean).

Cascadia subduction zone is a long [convergent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convergent_boundary) [plate boundary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plate_boundary), about off the Pacific coast of North America, that stretches from northern [Vancouver Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Island) in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada) to [Northern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_California) in the United States.
Case hardening is a [weathering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weathering) phenomenon of rock surface [induration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Induration).

Casma Group () is a [stratigraphic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(stratigraphy)) of [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous) ([Albian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albian) to [Cenomanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cenomanian)) [sedimentary formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_formation)s exposed along the coast and within the [Cordillera Occidental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Occidental_(Peru)) near [Casma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casma), [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru).

Central Highlands of Florida is a [geomorphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geomorphology) region of ridges, elevated areas called uplands, and valleys that extend up the center of the [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida) peninsula from a point northwest of [Lake Okeechobee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Okeechobee) to northern Florida.

Central Highlands terrane in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland), also known as the Grampian terrane, is a sequence of early [Paleozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleozoic) [metamorphic rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphic_rock) containing many [igneous intrusions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_intrusion).

Central Lapland Greenstone Belt (CLGB) is a [greenstone belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenstone_belt) located in the northern part of the [Fennoscandian Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fennoscandian_Shield).
Montana Alkalic Province is located in the United States in central [Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana).

Central Mountain Region () is a [physiogeographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiogeographical) region encompassing the central and eastern edge of [Albania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania).
Central Plain Group is a [geologic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(geology)) in [Antigua and Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda).

Central Russian Upland (also: Middle Russian Upland () and East European Upland) is an [upland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_(geography)) area of the [East European Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_European_Plain) and is an undulating plateau with an average elevation of .

Central Skåne Volcanic Province was a site of volcanic activity in the [Scania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scania) region of Sweden during the [Mesozoic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesozoic) [Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Era_(geology)) of the Earth's geological history.

central Swedish ice-edge zone was formed when the melting of [inland ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_sheet) slowed during a cold period approximately 12,000 years ago and the ice edge stood relatively still for around 800 years.

definition: Listwanite (also sometimes spelled listvenite, listvanite, or listwaenite) is a rock type that forms when the groundmass of [ultramafic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultramafic) rocks, most commonly mantle [peridotite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peridotite)s, is partially altered to carbonate minerals and cut by ubiquitous carbonate veins containing one or more of [magnesite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnesite), [calcite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcite), [dolomite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolomite_(mineral)), [ankerite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankerite), and/or [siderite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siderite).

Lithalsa is a [frost-induced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frost_heave) raised land form in [permafrost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permafrost) areas with mineral-rich soils, where a perennial [ice lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_lens) has developed within the soil.

Lithic sandstones, or lithic arenites, or litharenites, are [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone)s with a significant ( [[Category:Sedimentary rocks]] [[Category:Sandstone]] jqwgacqy22aa8oehytzgbwblqnuv17x

Lithification (from the [Ancient Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek) word lithos meaning 'rock' and the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin)-derived suffix -ific) is the process in which [sediment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sediment)s compact under [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure), expel [connate fluids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connate_fluids), and gradually become solid rock.
Lithiophosphate is a natural form of (pure) [lithium orthophosphate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium_orthophosphate).

Lithium Triangle () is a region of the [Andes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes) that is rich in [lithium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium) reserves, encompassed by the borders of [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina), [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia), and [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile).
Lithophagy is an ingestion of [stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone)s.

Lithoprobe was a Canadian national geoscience research project funded by the [Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_Sciences_and_Engineering_Research_Council) from 1984 to 2005, and one of the largest geoscientific research programs in Canadian history.

Lithos is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal), publishing original research papers on the [petrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrology), [geochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geochemistry) and [petrogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrogenesis) of [igneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_rock) and [metamorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphic_rock) rocks.

Lithostratigraphy is a sub-discipline of [stratigraphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratigraphy), the [geological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) [science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science) associated with the study of [strata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum) or rock layers.

Little Belt Mountains are a section of the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains) in the [U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) state of [Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana).
Little Falls Formation or Little Falls Dolostone is a [geologic formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(stratigraphy)) in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state)).

definition: Little Pinnacle, also known as The Haystack or Turf Rickrock, is a sea stack located off [Ballard Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballard_Down) on the [Isle of Purbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Purbeck) in [Dorset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorset), southern England.
Little Valley Formation is a [geologic formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(geology)) in [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia), United States.

definition: littoral cone is a type of [volcanic cone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_cone) formed from the interaction between [lava flows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_flows) and water.

Livradois () is a [natural region in France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_France) located in the center of the [Massif Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_Central), within the [departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_France) of [Puy-de-Dôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puy-de-Dôme) and [Haute-Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute-Loire).

Lizard complex, [Cornwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornwall) is generally accepted to represent a preserved example of an exposed [ophiolite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophiolite) complex in the United Kingdom.

Ljusdal Batholith is a group of [pluton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pluton_(geology))s in central Sweden formed during the [Svecofennian orogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svecofennian_orogeny).

definition: Llanbedrog Volcanic Group is an [Ordovician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordovician) [lithostratigraphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithostratigraphy) [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(stratigraphy)) (a sequence of [rock strata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_strata)) in northwest [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales).
Llandeilo Group is the middle subdivision of the British [Ordovician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordovician) rocks.

Llanite is a [porphyritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porphyritic) [rhyolite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhyolite) with distinctive blue [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz) and reddish [microcline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcline) [feldspar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feldspar) [phenocrysts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenocrysts) found in the [Llano Uplift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Llano_Uplift) north of [Llano, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Llano,_Texas), and dated at 1.1 [bya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bya).
Llano de Chocolate Beds is a geological unit of [sedimentary rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock) in Atacama Region of Chile.

Llewelyn Volcanic Group is an [Ordovician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordovician) [lithostratigraphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithostratigraphy) [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(stratigraphy)) (a sequence of [rock strata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_strata)) in [Snowdonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia), north-west [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales).

Lobate debris aprons (LDAs) are geological features on [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars), first seen by the [Viking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_program) Orbiters, consisting of piles of rock debris below cliffs.
Local Data Manager (LDM) is a suite of programs for the distribution of near real-time atmospheric earth data to researchers and educators free of charge as it becomes available.

Local Geodiversity Action Plan is a plan which sets out actions to conserve, enhance and promote the [geodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geodiversity) of a particular area, usually based along [local authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_authority) boundaries such as a [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County).

lode is a [deposit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deposition_(geology)) of [[wikt:metalliferous|metalliferous]] [ore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ore) that fills or is embedded in a [fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fracture_(geology)) (or crack) in a [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_(geology)) [formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geological_formation) or a [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein_(geology)) of ore that is deposited or embedded between [layers of rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum).
Lodestones are naturally [magnetized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetization) pieces of the mineral [magnetite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetite).

Loess (, ; from ) is a [clastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clastic_rock), predominantly [silt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silt)-sized [sediment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sediment) that is formed by the accumulation of wind-blown [dust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust).
log jam is a naturally occurring phenomenon characterized by a dense accumulation of tree trunks and pieces of large wood across a vast section of a river, stream, or lake.

Puerto Rico Trench is located on the boundary between the North [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean) and [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea), parallel to and north of [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Puerto_Rico), where the [oceanic trench](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_trench) reaches the deepest points in the Atlantic Ocean.

Puerto Rico–Virgin Islands microplate (PRVI), also known as the Puerto Rico–Virgin Islands block, is a [tectonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tectonics) [[List of tectonic plates#Microplates|microplate]] formed at the boundary zone between the [Caribbean plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_plate) and the obliquely subducting [North American plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_plate).

Pukekohe East Explosion Crater, also known as the Pukekohe East Crater, is one of the best preserved and most prominent volcanoes of the [South Auckland volcanic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Auckland_volcanic_field) in New Zealand.

pull-apart basin is a [structural basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_basin) where two overlapping (en echelon) [[fault (geology)#Strike-slip faults|strike-slip fault]]s or a fault bend create an area of [crustal extension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extensional_tectonics) undergoing [tension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tension_(geology)), which causes the basin to sink down.

Pulpí Geode (Spanish: Geoda de Pulpí) is a giant [geode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geode) found in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain) near the town of [Pulpí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulpí) ([Province of Almería](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Almería)) in December 1999, La geoda gigante de la Mina Rica (in Spanish)] *La Geoda de Pulpí website: https://www.geodapulpi.es/ [[Category:Rocks]] [[Category:Geology of Spain]] trtpou2qa39cxjxtgxt12a7gt4molg5

definition: Pyrobitumen is a type of solid, [amorphous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amorphous) organic matter.

pyroclastic fall deposit is a uniform deposit of material which has been ejected from a [volcanic eruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_eruption) or plume such as an ash fall or [tuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuff).
pyroclastic shield or ignimbrite shield is an uncommon type of [shield volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shield_volcano).
pyroclastic surge is a fluidised mass of turbulent gas and rock fragments that is ejected during some [volcanic eruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_eruption)s.
Pyrolite is a term used to characterize a model composition of the Earth's [mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_mantle_(Earth)).

Pyrometamorphism is a type of [metamorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphism) in which rocks are rapidly changed by heat, e.g. coming from a rapidly emplaced extrusive or intrusive igneous rock or from a fossil fuel fire.

Pyroxenite is an [ultramafic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultramafic) [igneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous) [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_(geology)) consisting essentially of [mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral)s of the [pyroxene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyroxene) group, such as [augite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augite), [diopside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diopside), [hypersthene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypersthene), [bronzite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronzite) or [enstatite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enstatite).

definition: quartz arenite or quartzarenite is a [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone) composed of greater than 90% [detrital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detrital) [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz).

Quartz diorite is an [igneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_rock), plutonic ([intrusive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock)) [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_(geology)), of [felsic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felsic) composition, with [phaneritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phanerite) texture.

Quartz gabbro is an [intrusive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock) with a composition intermediate between [gabbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabbro) and [tonalite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonalite).

Quartz monzogabbro is an [intrusive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock) intermediate between [quartz gabbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz_gabbro) and [quartz monzonite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz_monzonite).

Quartz monzonite is an [intrusive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock), [felsic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felsic), [igneous rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_rock) that has an approximately equal proportion of [orthoclase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthoclase) and [plagioclase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagioclase) [feldspar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feldspar)s.

Quartz dolerite or quartz diabase is an [intrusive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock) similar to [dolerite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabase) (also called diabase), but with an excess of [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz).

Quartz-porphyry, in layman's terms, is a type of volcanic ([igneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_rocks)) rock containing large [porphyritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porphyritic) crystals of [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz).

Quartzite is a hard, non-[foliated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foliation_(geology)) [metamorphic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphic_rock) that was originally pure [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz) [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone).

Quartzolite or silexite is an [intrusive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_rock) [igneous rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igneous_rock), in which the [mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral) [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz) is more than 90% of the rock's [felsic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felsic) mineral content, with [feldspar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feldspar) at up to 10%.
Quaternary geology is the branch of [geology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) that study developments from 2.58 million years ago to the present.

Quaternary science is the subfield of [geology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) which studies the [Quaternary Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary_Period), commonly known as the [ice age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_age).

Quebrada Marquesa Formation (Spanish: Formación Quebrada Marquesa) is a [geological formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geological_formation) composed of alternations of volcanic and [volcaniclastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcaniclastic) rock layers and mostly continental (as opposed to marine) sedimanry rocks in inland [Coquimbo Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coquimbo_Region), northern [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile).

Queen Charlotte triple junction is a geologic [triple junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_junction) where three [tectonic plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tectonic_plate)s meet: the [Pacific plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_plate), the [North American plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_plate), and the [Explorer plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explorer_plate).

Stylolites (Greek: stylos, pillar; lithos, stone) are serrated surfaces within a [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_(geology)) mass at which [mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral) material has been removed by [pressure dissolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure_solution), in a deformation process that decreases the total volume of rock.

sub-Cambrian peneplain is an ancient, extremely flat, erosion surface ([peneplain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peneplain)) that has been exhumed and exposed by erosion from under [Cambrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambrian) [strata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strata) over large swathes of [Fennoscandia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fennoscandia).
subaerial unconformity is a surface that displays signs of [erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erosion) by processes that commonly occur on the surface.

subbasin or sub-basin is a structural [geologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) feature where a larger [basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_basin) is divided into a series of smaller basins with intervening intrabasinal highs.
Subboreal is a [climatic period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleoclimatology), immediately before the present one, the [subatlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatlantic) period.

Subduction is a geological process in which the [oceanic lithosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithosphere) and some continental lithosphere is [recycled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geochemical_cycle) into the [Earth's mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth's_mantle) at the [convergent boundaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convergent_boundary) between tectonic plates.

Tectonic erosion or subduction erosion is the loss of [crust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crust_(geology)) from an [overriding tectonic plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tectonic_plate) due to [subduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subduction).
subduction tectonics of the Philippines is the control of geology over the [Philippine archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_archipelago).

subglacial mound is a type of [subglacial volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subglacial_volcano) formed when [lava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava) erupts beneath a thick [glacier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacier) or [ice sheet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_sheet).
subgrain rotation recrystallization is recognized as an important mechanism for [dynamic recrystallisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_recrystallisation).

submarine, undersea, or underwater earthquake is an [earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake) that occurs [underwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underwater) at the [bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabed) of a [body of water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_of_water), especially an [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean).

Submarine landslides are [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [landslide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide)s that [transport sediment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sediment_transport) across the [continental shelf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelf) and into the [deep ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_sea).

Submersion is the sustainable cyclic portion of [coastal erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_erosion) where coastal sediments move from the visible portion of a [beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach) to the submerged near[shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shore) region, and later return to the original visible portion of the beach.
Subsea production systems are typical wells located on the [seabed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabed), shallow or deep water.

Sylacauga marble, also commonly known as Alabama marble, is a [marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marble) that is found in a belt running through [Talladega County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talladega_County,_Alabama).

Sylvinite is a [sedimentary rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock) made of a mechanical mixture of the minerals [sylvite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvite) (KCl, or [potassium chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potassium_chloride)) and [halite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halite) (NaCl, or [sodium chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium_chloride)).

syncline is a [fold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(geology)) with younger layers closer to the center of the structure, whereas an [anticline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticline) is the inverse of a syncline.

Syngenetic permafrost growth is a mode of the growth of [permafrost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permafrost) whereby additional material is deposited to a permafrost site during freezing conditions, causing the permafrost layer to build upwards.

Syngman Rhee Line () was a marine boundary line established by [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Republic_of_South_Korea)n President [Syngman Rhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syngman_Rhee) in his [[Category:Liancourt Rocks]] [[Category:Syngman Rhee]] [[Category:Territorial disputes of Japan]] [[Category:Territorial disputes of South Korea]] 44569klmu3hfia97fwe95dypq7lj4od

SYNOP (surface synoptic observations) is a numerical [code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code) (called FM-12 by [WMO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization)) used for reporting [weather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather) observations made by staffed and [automated weather stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_weather_station).

syntaxis is an abrupt major change in the dominant orientation of the main [fold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(geology)) and [thrust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrust_fault) structures in an [orogenic belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orogenic_belt).

Synthetic alexandrite is an artificially grown [crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal)line variety of [chrysoberyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysoberyl), composed of [beryllium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryllium) aluminum oxide (BeAlO).

synthetic seismogram is the result of forward modelling the [seismic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflection_seismology) response of an input earth model, which is defined in terms of 1D, 2D, or 3D variations in physical properties.

Syrian Arc is a series of [fold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(geology)) structures that extend from Syria, through [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon) and [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)/[Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region)) into northern [Sinai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula) and on into [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)'s [Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Desert) and [Western desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Desert_(Egypt))s.

system in [stratigraphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratigraphy) is a sequence of [strata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum) (rock layers) that were laid down together within the same corresponding [geological period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_(geology)).

Systems geology emphasizes the nature of [geology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology) as a [system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System) – that is, as a set of interacting parts that function as a whole.

Szydłowiec sandstone ([Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_language): piaskowiec szydłowiecki) is a variation of fine-grained and medium-grained [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone) present in the area around the town of [Szydłowiec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szydłowiec), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland).
